candidates.exact_span: Regulations contained in 40 CFR §122.44 requires that NPDES permit limits are developed that meet the more stringent of either technology-based effluent limitation guidelines, numerical and/or narrative water quality standard-based effluent limits, or the previous permit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Different readings of the 'more stringent of' selection rule could change which numeric or narrative limit is treated as the applicable enforceable limit for a given parameter and discharge point.

candidates.exact_span: Effluent limitations established at Outfall 001 in the current permit regulate overflows from Quarry #1 pond which stores storm runoff and process water effluent from plant areas.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of which discharges and sources are covered at Outfall 001 affects which limits and monitoring obligations attach to reported measurements or missing-evidence cases for that outfall.

candidates.exact_span: The 40 CFR 411.37 ELG of 50 mg/l was the basis for establishment of TSS effluent limitation at Outfall 001.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether this 50 mg/l ELG is read as the operative enforceable TSS limit at Outfall 001 directly determines the numeric threshold used for compliance comparison.

candidates.exact_span: EPA did not establish 40 CFR 411.13 temperature limitation at Outfall 001 because discharges at Outfall 001 would be intermittent and the permit restricted discharges due to catastrophic or chronic precipitation events.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether temperature is an applicable enforceable limit (A), whether discharge-occurrence or event-based conditions alter monitoring requirements (B), and whether intermittent or precipitation-restricted discharge periods explain absent results versus required monitoring (C) all hinge on this passage.

candidates.exact_span: The 40 CFR 411.17 TSS mass load limitation might not be applicable at Outfall 001 because the combination of storm runoff and process water.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether the mass-load TSS limit is treated as applicable versus inapplicable changes which numeric limit, if any, governs TSS compliance at Outfall 001.

candidates.exact_span: TSS reported maximum daily discharge did exceed the daily max limit of 50 mg/l.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of whether the daily maximum 50 mg/l limit is the operative comparison metric—and whether this historical exceedance is treated as establishing an enforceable daily-max standard—affects which limit basis is applied in compliance evaluation.

candidates.exact_span: As a result, it is proposed in the draft permit that the permittee report 30-day average for TSS.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether the proposed 30-day average reporting obligation is treated as an enforceable monitoring and/or averaging requirement changes applicable monitoring obligations (B) and whether compliance is evaluated against a daily maximum or a 30-day average limit (A).

candidates.exact_span: Water quality-based requirements are necessary where effluent limits more stringent than technology-based limits are necessary to maintain or achieve federal or state water quality limits.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Different readings of when water quality-based limits supersede technology-based limits could change which numeric or narrative limit is selected as the applicable enforceable limit.
